i.norm:
Tests {@link ExtraFieldUtils#parse} when told to {@code READ} extra-field blocks that it cannot fully parse.

Each ZIP extra field is laid out as: 

 [ header id : 2 bytes ][ data length : 2 bytes ][ data : <data length> bytes ]

The test data concatenates two such fields back to back:

  1. a recognized {@link AsiExtraField} (a Unix-permissions field), and
  2. an unrecognized field whose header id is not known to Commons Compress.
Size in bytes of the header-id portion of an extra field.

Size in bytes of an extra field's fixed prefix (header id + data length).

Expected Unix mode of the directory entry: octal 0755 with the directory flag set.
Concatenated local-file-data bytes of {@link #asiField} followed by {@link #unrecognizedField}.
A recognized extra field: a directory with Unix permissions 0755.
An extra field whose header id is unknown to Commons Compress.
Serializes the given fields into a single byte array using the local-file-data layout ({@code header id | data length | data} per field).
Complete data: both fields are well-formed, so the unrecognized field is returned as an UnrecognizedExtraField holding its single data byte.

Truncated data: drop the very last byte so the second field's declared length exceeds the bytes actually present. With READ, the leftover bytes are captured verbatim as an UnparseableExtraFieldData instead of being parsed.
The unparseable holder keeps the 4 trailing bytes (header id + length of the truncated second field) exactly as they appeared in the input.
